capabilities: Copy PDF selections as citation-style links
Import annotations from Zotero, Kindle, Apple Books, and Apple Preview
Insert Zotero or vault citations and update reference lists
Annotate DOCX and text files through Markdown discussion threads
Fill empty reading-note properties from PDF metadata
disambiguation: Not a handwriting transcription tool; ink annotations are preserved as entries but not converted to text.
extras: Retains PDF++'s private PDF viewer compatibility layer; direct PDF editing can modify vault PDFs and needs backups; handwriting OCR and Google Docs comment import are not implemented.
intentEvidence: This is still a PDF++ fork, not a replacement for Zotero.
motivation: The author wanted copied PDF links to read like citations and keep scholarly notes quieter while preserving PDF++'s backlink highlighting.
problem: PDF annotations and copied links in Obsidian expose technical file and page details and are disconnected from citation metadata and reading-app highlights.

relations.evidence: PDF Scholia Scribe is a maintained fork of PDF++
Zotero is used for citation metadata and formatted references

summary: PDF++ fork for citation-style PDF links, Zotero and reading-app annotation import, DOCX annotation threads, and reference lists.
